status: AUTHORED AND NOT ACTIVE, 2026-10-01. Ready to paste into data/gulch_mine.json as its `farms`, `farms_why` and `farms_grid` keys. Held out of that file because switching the farms on activates the raw-stone DROP ROLL, a generator path that had never been generated (the file has never had a farms key), and the gulch's test surface is written to assert that path is dormant: tests/test_gulch_redesign_independent.py has a test named test_the_drop_roll_is_inert_without_a_farm_den. With these farms in place the gulch suites go 12 red and tests/test_system_contracts.py 3 red (C12 once, C14 twice, gulch_megas reapproach and restart), because tests/gulch_sim.py's world model has no NBT storage model and the roll is built on storage. NONE of those reds is a fault in this data: the farms' own audit is clean. They are a test surface that must be rewritten BY A TEST AUTHOR -- not by the hand that wrote this data -- and that author needs the canonical heightmap, which an agent's isolation worktree never receives. So it is a main-session unit, and it is the only thing between this and the world.
why_it_was_authored_anyway: The sites cost a real heightmap scan and the schema cost a real read of tools/gulch_mine.py. Both are written down here so the next session pastes and builds rather than re-deriving. Verified before it was parked: `python tools/gulch_mine.py build` emits all seven farms (zone advancements, zone and turn_back functions, bind/gone/spawn keeper functions per den), and `python tools/gulch_mine_audit.py` is CLEAN at 0 problems with the farms in place.
owner_decision_still_open: The zone. Each farm here gets a 41-block square round its den's pad and nothing more, so the Mega is SEEN from outside and not reached -- the cordon language the Deep already uses -- with the turn-back yaw facing the den so a player put out looks straight back at what turned them. The alternative is no zone at all, letting the level band (60 outer, 67 deeper against a cap of 50) be the only gate. The owner asked that 'the gates stay as designed', which is why the zone is here, but a turn-back in open country is a different thing from one at a rockslide and they may not want it.
farms_why: The open-air Mega farms (the owner, 2026-10-01): 'Mega Pokemon walking in the OPEN, not only in caverns -- a player should see them before they reach them.' Seven dens across the Rift's two southern arms, four outer and three deeper, keeping the material chain, the Cutters and the gates exactly as designed: a den's Mega rolls the same raw-stone drop at its tier's rate, the keyed stone is still cut at the Cutters, and each den is still behind the same badge flag. What changes is that the fight is on open ground a player can see across, not in a hall they have to be let into. The halls' two Megas (megas.slots) stay as they are: the owner said not ONLY in caverns. Sites measured off the canonical heightmap, never a world (CLAUDE.md): inside the arm polygons of data/regions.json, pad slope under 10 degrees, 24+ clear of every keep_clear box, 260+ apart so finding one is an event rather than a checklist. The sightline measurement that chose them saturated at its own 136-block ceiling for all twelve candidates, so it proves each has a long clear approach and did NOT rank them: spacing and arm coverage picked these seven. The east arm holds the gulch, its road and the Cutters, so it carries the outer tier; the west arm had nothing in it at all, so it carries the deeper tier and the longest walk.

farms_grid.why: The box the farms' ANCHORS, turn-back points and approach boxes live in -- not a block box. The farms write no blocks at all: a den is a keeper line, a leash line, a zone advancement and a turn-back, and nothing in them places a single block. `grid` stays exactly as tight as it was, because it guards block writes and must keep doing so; widening it to admit these coordinates would have weakened the one guard that keeps this build inside its box, and a threshold widened to make data pass is not a threshold (CLAUDE.md). So the audit checks block writes against `grid` and farm coordinates against this.

farms.name: the East Arm shoulder

zone.why: A 41-square round the den's pad, not the whole arm. The owner wants the Mega SEEN before it is reached, so the zone is the pad a player would stand on to fight it and nothing more: from outside it the Mega is in plain sight across open ground, and the turn-back point 52 blocks E is still in view of it. A zone over the arm would hide what it is meant to advertise. The turn-back yaw faces the den, not away from it: a player put out of the pad looks straight back at the Mega, which is what makes it a cordon rather than a dead end.

dens.why: Mega Aggron: steel and rock, the arm's own stone. Aron and Lairon are the Mining Town's fossil levels, so a player meets the line before the Mega
dens.leash_why: 32, not the halls' 24: the owner asked for Megas WALKING in the open, so a den's Mega roams twice the radius a cavern slot does before the keeper puts it back.
dens.model_not_verified: The Mega form's client model is not verified for this species, the same caveat data/gulch_mine.json already records for excadrill (M-7). A missing model shows a player a default, it does not break the fight.

farms.why: One den per farm, because the dens are 260+ blocks apart by construction and one zone cannot be tight around all of them at once.
